bull.t: Recurring membership economics and high retention
bull.b: Costco’s membership model provides recurring subscription revenue alongside merchandise sales, while high renewal rates indicate strong customer loyalty. Rising executive-member penetration and a growing cardholder base can support repeat visits, larger baskets, and durable earnings quality.

bull.t: Digital growth and expanding omnichannel reach
bull.b: Rapid digital sales growth broadens Costco’s reach beyond warehouse visits and strengthens convenience for existing members. Expanded delivery coverage, rising digital engagement, and incremental online shopping trips can support durable sales growth while reinforcing the membership proposition.

bull.t: Strong balance sheet and cash generation
bull.b: Material deleveraging improves financial resilience and gives Costco greater flexibility to fund warehouse expansion, digital infrastructure, and shareholder distributions. Growing operating and free cash flow also supports reinvestment without relying as heavily on external financing.

bear.t: Gross-margin pressure and higher inventory costs
bear.b: Costco’s low-markup model leaves profitability sensitive to merchandise mix, inflation, and inventory-cost changes. Faster growth in gas, e-commerce, and pharmacy, together with higher LIFO charges, can constrain margin expansion even when sales growth remains strong.

Slower membership growth could moderate one of Costco’s most valuable recurring revenue streams and reduce the pace of future traffic expansion. Although retention remains strong, normalization makes continued warehouse openings and member acquisition more important to sustaining growth.

Regulated and changing drug pricing can pressure pharmacy economics and reduce the contribution from a growing ancillary business. Double-digit prescription growth has offset the initial impact, but continued pricing changes may limit the durability of pharmacy-led revenue and profit gains.
